text:
sanjay: Running the scheduled repo leak-scan and found an AWS access key in a pipeline artifact for repo `infra/terraform-modules`. It appears in build log from job 4821 (artifact cache). snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T11:12:34Z] exporting AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAEXAMPLExx1234
[2026-03-15T11:12:34Z] using profile developer
```
Not sure if it's a deploy key or a service account. Flagging.

olivia: ack. moving to incident channel? we should revoke ASAP and start audit. :rotating_light:

maya: do we have the exact job id and artifact URL? can we identify when that key was created? cloudtrail will help.

sanjay: job id 4821 on gitlab-runner-02, artifact url: https://gitlab.redwood/infra/-/jobs/4821/artifacts/download. Detected by gitleaks scan run by cron. Looks like a long-lived key created 2025-11-02 per iam console.

ci-bot: [automated] leak-scan alert: repo=infra/terraform-modules, path=.gitlab-ci.yml, job=4821, match=AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY pattern

leo: I'll take containment: rotate/revoke the key now. olivia, can you check which services used it? Maya, check CloudTrail for last `AssumeRole` or `sts:AssumeRole` and KMS decrypts.

olivia: revocation in progress. IAM console shows the key attached to user `ci-deploy` used by onprem-runner. Disabling now. After disable, create replacement and map runner to new short-lived creds via KMS+OIDC. ETA 15m.

maya: querying CloudTrail... last use 2026-03-14T09:47:12Z from runner ip 34.210.12.8. No signs of suspicious external access but we need full scan. I'll pull S3 access logs for that timeframe and KMS decrypt logs for any decrypts using that principal.

sanjay: also need to purge artifact cache containing the secret and any historic artifacts. gitlab has object storage; we should delete that artifact. leo, can you trigger artifact purge and invalidate caches?

leo: purged artifacts for job 4821 and invalidated runner cache for infra/terraform-modules. Added emergency commit to remove the literal from history and instructed devs to rotate any local copies.

olivia: created new key with limited perms and rotated in our secrets manager. Pushed CI change to use KMS-encrypted secrets fetched at runtime using instance role. Also filed a dedicated ticket to migrate all runners to OIDC-based short-lived creds.

maya: audit notes: no KMS decrypts found by that key in last 90 days, looks like used for infra state exports once/week. However we saw several terraform `plan` runs touching prod buckets — marking for post-incident review.

sanjay: next steps: (1) postmortem + timeline, (2) run full gitleaks/trufflehog across all repos and build logs, (3) enforce gitlab runner RBAC changes and require OIDC via ticket #SEC-712, (4) add artifact retention policy and auto-purge on secret matches.

olivia: notifying legal & customer-support for potential disclosure? probably not required but FYI.

maya: I'll prepare CloudTrail + KMS logs export and attach to incident. Also recommend adding key rotation policy and removing long-lived IAM keys for any CI users. 

leo: adding rule to our CI linting to fail if `AWS_` env var appears in printed logs or artifacts. Also enabling audit logging on runners.

sanjay: good work team. I'll open the postmortem doc and assign action items. Please add any further findings here. :white_check_mark:
